title: setDesiredAPY commit branch does not clear pendingAPYBps / pendingAPYBlockNumber, leaving inert-but-misleading view state
rootCause: After a successful commit (lines 163-171), the function clears `apySetInProgress` but leaves `pendingAPYBps` and `pendingAPYBlockNumber` populated with the just-committed values. These are read by the public view `getPendingAPYInfo()` and by integrators monitoring the two-step intent flow. Since the gate logic correctly keys off `apySetInProgress`, the stale fields do not affect future commits, but they DO mislead any integrator that polls `getPendingAPYInfo()` thinking a pending preview is still queued.
impact: Front-end / governance-dashboard confusion. No fund loss, no protocol-state corruption. Strictly QA. Notable because off-chain monitors built around the documented two-step preview-then-commit flow will misreport state until the next preview overwrites the fields.
steps: owner.setDesiredAPY(500) again within 100 blocks -- commit branch fires; desiredAPYBps=500; apySetInProgress=false.
Integrators reading only the first two fields incorrectly infer that another preview is queued.
remediation: Add `pendingAPYBps = 0; pendingAPYBlockNumber = 0;` at the end of the commit branch.
profileReference: Profile §4.1 setDesiredAPY note: 'pendingAPYBps and pendingAPYBlockNumber are NOT zeroed on commit'.
